caption_or_description: Light emitted in the water is partly refracted and partly reflected at the surface. The blue dashed lines show the direction of light and the lengths of the arrows indicate the proportions refracted and reflected. Beyond the critical angle, the beam is totally internally reflected.
An observer underwater sees a circle of light at the still surface. Beyond a cone of 96 degrees (twice the critical angle), an observer sees a reflection of the water interior or bottom.
notes: Caption uses degree symbol in HTML.

caption_or_description: Total internal reflection in a prism. The prism changes the direction of the light beam (a) by 90 degrees, (b) by 180 degrees, and (c) not at all. Note that, in each case, the orientation of the image is different from the orientation of the object.
notes: Caption uses degree symbols in HTML.

caption_or_description: Total internal reflection in a pair of prisms, common in binoculars.
Paths of light in a diamond. Rays that strike the inner surface at angles larger than the critical angle are internally reflected and exit via refraction at the top surface.
The light is piped from below by a succession of total internal reflections until it emerges at the top ends.
notes: Caption quotation marks restored in HTML.

caption_or_description: A lens may be thought of as a set of blocks and prisms: (a) a converging lens and (b) a diverging lens.
notes: Captured image exists but belongs to Section 28.7, not 28.6.
